children: Barratt Redrow's latest update suggests the home builder should be resilient enough to ride out the current macroeconomic backdrop, AJ Bell analyst Russ Mould says. Its strong balance sheet and the continuing benefits from Redrow's integration are clear positives for the market to take away despite Barratt downgrading sales forecasts due mostly to planning delays, he says. This is something the industry has consistently complained about, but the issues may not get much of a hearing ahead of the budget given the competing demands the U.K. treasury chief is having to weigh, he says. "What Barratt needs is a shift in the geopolitical and macroeconomic backdrop which would allow for an easing of borrowing costs, boosting the availability and affordability of mortgages," Mould says. Shares are up 8.8% at 300.70 pence (anthony.orunagoriainoff@dowjones.com)
